handfixes.summary: XERO_TENANT_ID is sourced into the per-request Headers map (Xero-Tenant-Id header on every call)
handfixes.why: Xero requires the Xero-Tenant-Id header on EVERY call alongside the bearer token. The env-var wiring (XERO_TENANT_ID -> Headers) is hand-wired in config.go and pinned by config_auth_test.go; a reprint drops it and every call 401/403s.

handfixes.summary: 5 of 7 resource primary-key fields are hand-wired (accounts/items templated; the rest hand-set)
handfixes.why: Xero's per-resource ID field names (BankTransactionID, ContactID, InvoiceID, JournalID, PaymentID) are hand-wired for ExtractResourceID; the generator only templated accounts/items. Pinned by TestExtractResourceID_Xero. A reprint reverts the five to a generic guess and breaks sync key extraction.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For xero the manifest gained: XERO_AUTHORIZATION_URL, XERO_BASE_URL, XERO_CLIENT_ID, XERO_CLIENT_SECRET, XERO_TENANT_ID, XERO_TOKEN_URL. server.json gained: XERO_AUTHORIZATION_URL, XERO_BASE_URL, XERO_CLIENT_ID, XERO_CLIENT_SECRET, XERO_OAUTH2, XERO_TENANT_ID, XERO_TOKEN_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: XERO_AUTHORIZATION_URL, XERO_BASE_URL, XERO_CLIENT_ID, XERO_CLIENT_SECRET, XERO_TENANT_ID, XERO_TOKEN_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: XERO_NO_CONFIG_WRITE makes every credential write a no-op (token cache included) while leaving the `auth logout` erase working, and the MCP server honours it too (issue #270)
handfixes.why: Issue #270, raised by @Xenith-B off the back of #266. #266 stopped env-supplied client credentials reaching disk; the MINTED access token still landed in ~/.config/<tool>-cli/config.toml in cleartext and there was no supported way to turn that off. Their workaround was `--config NUL`, which is OS-specific, undocumented, makes doctor report a false 'not configured', and - the part that matters most - does not cover the MCP servers at all, because internal/mcp resolved its own hardcoded config path and ignored --config. Three deliberate boundaries make this switch honest rather than merely quiet. (1) ClearTokens keeps calling save() directly: it is the ERASE path, and routing it through the guard would make `auth logout` silently inert, which is a worse defect than the one being fixed. (2) `auth login`, the only command on this connector that writes a credential on purpose (its `auth --help` lists login, logout, setup, status), REFUSES and names the variable rather than reporting a save that did not happen - a false success is the same defect class as a doctor that says credentials are fine without checking. (3) newMCPClient now resolves through config.Load(""), the resolver the CLI uses, so the MCP server honours both XERO_CONFIG and this switch; that is the half the issue says is uncovered today. The variable is declared on all three install channels because for a Claude Desktop install the manifest prompt is the ONLY channel that can set an environment variable. Class C, new documented surface. GENERATOR-class: a reprint drops the switch entirely and silently restores the plaintext token cache.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit <PREFIX>_NO_CONFIG_WRITE (or an equivalent) as part of the standard config surface, with the same three boundaries: the erase path exempt, explicit save commands failing loudly rather than no-oping, and the MCP server resolving its config through config.Load("") instead of a hardcoded home-relative path. The hardcoded path in internal/mcp/tools.go is a generator defect in its own right - it makes --config and <PREFIX>_CONFIG inert for every MCP install on every connector.

asserts.contains: | `auth login` | Refuses, naming the variable, instead of reporting a save that did not happen. |

handfixes.summary: One decoded output funnel for every server text the client shows: maskCredentialText (every API error, transport error, displayed URL and --dry-run parameter goes through it) still masks each held credential as written and URL-escaped, then withholds the WHOLE text if any held value survives in any view reachable by undoing control/format characters, JSON and JavaScript escapes, percent escapes at any depth, HTML entities, markup tags, and base64/base64url/hex runs at every alignment (cliutil.FunnelWithhold, shared byte-identical across the fleet). The held set is every value the masks cover plus the part after a scheme word and both halves of a base64 id:secret pair (Basic auth, composed keys). Surfaces funnelled here: the API error body (checked whole before the 4096-byte display cut, then again as shown); the token refresh endpoint's error body. Round 3 (owner-approved structural pass): the decoder searches every view breadth-first over one fixed set of steps (control-character drop, JSON and JavaScript escapes, the identity escape as its own step, percent, HTML entities, tag strip, base64 at four alignments, hex at two), matches every view, the original included, before any filter, keeps every view a step makes (a literal backslash survives), deduplicates, and is capped by total work (512 times the input plus 4 MiB; text over 1 MiB or past the cap is withheld). Every value a funnel call is given is held process-wide (cliutil.FunnelHold), and the client holds its credentials when built and its resolved auth header on every request. Two error-only backstops withhold any held value: every command error before Cobra prints it plus every JSON/agent error envelope (internal/cli/secret_funnel_cli.go), and every MCP error result and handler error through the outermost tool middleware (cmd/<mcp>/secret_funnel_mcp.go). Success output is never funnelled. The `auth login` code exchange funnels the complete raw body with the client secret and authorization code before it prints the decoded error object.
handfixes.why: class_harness.py secret-echo (Step 3.1, PR #436) drives the built CLI and MCP server against a fake server that reflects each configured credential in every encoding; on origin/main this connector printed the credential HTML-entity-encoded, JSON-escaped, double URL-encoded or base64 (the generated masks cover only the raw, QueryEscape and PathEscape forms; press issue #5145). Matching encoded needles one at a time never converged (saas-alerts and cisco-meraki review loops), so the fix is a decode-then-check backstop that withholds the whole text and fails closed (text over 4 MiB, a decoding chain that does not settle in 32 rounds, or work past the budget is withheld). Classification is kept: the plain withheld notice avoids every word the auth-error classifiers match, and a withheld text that itself read as an auth failure gets a notice that says so (an HTTP 400 'invalid token' answer echoing the token keeps its auth exit code). Codex round 1 (2026-10-23) added that, the fail-closed depth bound (a text-like layer left at depth 8 withholds), the JavaScript escapes \v, \0 and the identity escape, a bounded \u{ search, and the token-endpoint error bodies outside the client. Known limits: values under 8 characters are only masked as written; case-changed, split-and-interleaved or otherwise transformed (compressed, encrypted) echoes are not reconstructed. A reprint that drops these edits fails class_harness.py secret-echo in CI and these asserts.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: cli-printing-press issue #5145 (encoded credential echo). The generated maskCredentialText should end in a decode-then-check backstop over every held credential, and the error-body and token-endpoint paths should check the whole body before the display cut.

handfixes.summary: every MCP tool not annotated read-only previews and sends only with confirm set to boolean true
handfixes.why: Work order 2026-11-02: an MCP write must preview and send only with confirm: true. One gate in internal/mcp/write_confirm.go wraps every tool the read-only switch would drop (same predicate), so a tool a future print adds without an annotation fails closed. The call sits in the generated tools.go; an mcp regeneration drops it silently.

handfixes.summary: XERO_OAUTH2 (the variable guide.md documents as the API credential) still becomes the Bearer token
handfixes.why: Press 4.35.1's AuthHeader reads only AccessToken, so an install configured with XERO_OAUTH2 (declared on all three install channels) silently sent no credential. Pinned by TestLegacyOauth2EnvStillRead.

handfixes.summary: runtime proof that a rejected token refresh returns on both entry paths (mint_lock_scan false-RED)
handfixes.why: fleet/bin/mint_lock_scan.py exits 1 on the native 4.35.1 client (maskHeldError masks with held=true and never re-takes lockTokenState). These tests drive invalid_grant before the call and after a 401 and fail on a deadlock; mutating maskHeldError to held=false makes them fail.

handfixes.summary: local analytics open the store read-only, count only AUTHORISED cash, never add across currencies, read payables as credits, take a payment's contact from its document, and date journals
handfixes.why: Codex 2026-11-02 rounds 1-2 on the novels, each against a shape Xero's OpenAPI documents: an MCP read created the store; DELETED payments and DELETED/VOIDED bank transactions counted as cash; USD and EUR summed into one total; CREDITORS (NetAmount negative) reported a -200 variance on a tied bill; payments carry no top-level Contact; journals carry only CreatedDateUTC. The novels are copied from the PUBLISHED tree on a reprint, so these pins stop an older copy coming back.

asserts.contains: func livePayment(p Payment) bool { return p.Status == "AUTHORISED" }

handfixes.summary: README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json say the ChatGPT desktop app runs this connector locally (STDIO) and that ChatGPT on the web, Microsoft 365 Copilot / Copilot Studio and the Gemini app are not supported by msp-skills yet, with a link to the hosted-gateway comparison; no paid-plan list, no Developer Mode recipe, no 'ChatGPT connects only to remote servers'.
handfixes.why: Docs fix approved 2026-11-03, following PR #502. OpenAI's MCP docs (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp) say the ChatGPT desktop app, Codex CLI and the IDE extension support MCP servers, add them as STDIO, and share MCP configuration; ChatGPT on the web uses remote MCP through plugins and does not read local Codex config. The old text listed ChatGPT plans, said ChatGPT connects only to remote servers, and on the reprinted connectors told users to host the connector over HTTPS for a Developer Mode connector and Copilot Studio; SECURITY.md pauses HTTP mode until each connector is reprinted. README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json are regenerated by msp-skills-publish onboard.py, whose template still writes the old ChatGPT text, so without this entry a re-onboard or reprint silently restores it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Change the ChatGPT, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Gemini app text in onboard.py (cc-skills msp-skills-publish) so a regeneration writes this wording itself, then this entry can be retired.

asserts.contains: **Not supported by msp-skills yet.** ChatGPT on the web

### Does this work with ChatGPT?

Yes, in the **ChatGPT desktop app**.

asserts.not_contains: Microsoft 365 Copilot, Gemini, and any agent
